subject: Oracle backend - need help with copy_to()

messages.author: af1128a04b090701
messages.subject: Oracle backend - need help with copy_to()
parts:
Hi,

I tried to add Oracle as a new backend to dplyr (https://github.com/tomasgreif/dplyr/tree/oracle). So far it works pretty well, however I don't know what to do with copy_to(). Anyone out there willing to help? @hadley - is there any chance this could be merged into dplyr once fixed or I will need to keep my dplyr clone separately?

Tomas


# Install
library(devtools)
install_github('tomasgreif/dplyr', ref = 'oracle')
library(dplyr)

# Connect (we have SIDs)
host <- "10.129.72.10"
port <- 1521
sid <- "ourdb"
connect.string <- paste(
  "(DESCRIPTION=",
  "(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=tcp)(HOST=", host, ")(PORT=", port, "))",
  "(CONNECT_DATA=(SID=", sid, ")))", sep = "")


# To connect to a database first create a src:
my_db <- src_oracle(username = "user", password = "password", 
                    dbname = connect.string)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Oracle backend - need help with copy_to()
parts:
Hi Tomas,

It's better to put it in a separate package - I'm going to keep
sqlite, mysql and postgres bindings in dplyr but everything else will
be separate.

Does the oracle db package not have a dbWriteTable function?

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Oracle backend - need help with copy_to()
parts:
Hi Hadley,

thank you, it was obvious - I copied src-postgres without thinking too much. Do you have any specific reasons for keeping Oracle out of dplyr? As you know there are more people trying to use Oracle with dplyr (e.g. https://github.com/datalove/dplyr/tree/oracle/R). It would be so much easier for all Oracle users to use dplyr than something called dplyrOracle. Is there anything I could do to change your mind? 

Tomas

you know it dplyr has a huge dependency list and it's really hard for
me to test. I've already moved the MonetDB backend out of dplyr, and
bigquery has a backend in its own package.

Hadley
